title: The data layer and the transport layer

videos.script: MCP has two layers. The data layer is the messages, JSON-RPC requests, results and errors. The transport layer is how those messages travel: lines on a pipe, or HTTP requests. {{title}} This lesson types the messages by hand. No model, no library on the client side: a request goes in, and whatever the server sends back is printed. {{byhand}} You will see what a modern request has to carry, and what the server says when it does not. You will see a tool that failed and a tool that did not exist, and how differently they come back. {{errors}} Then a request that needs a person halfway through. The server answers with a question, and the client asks again with the answer and a sealed token. Change one character of the token, and the server refuses it. {{mrtr}} And last, the two transports: why standard output belongs to the protocol, and what a Streamable HTTP server checks before it reads the body. {{last}}
